This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Hurricane Esai E.S. brought heavy rain and high winds when it made landfall near Pensacola, Florida last night.
Troy Public Radio's Kyle Gassett reports the Category 2 storm has weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it continues to make its way across Alabama.
Alabama Governor Kay Ivey closed state offices and ordered tourists to evacuate counties near the Gulf Coast.
We often hear in emergency management, "hope for the best, prepare for the worst."
Ivey also declared a state of emergency in 40 counties, including the state capital, Montgomery.
The declaration also triggered Alabama's price gouging law, making it illegal for businesses to sharply raise prices on gasoline and other essential goods during the emergency.
For NPR News, I'm Kyle Gassett in Montgomery, Alabama.
President Trump made a campaign stop in central New York last night to throw his support behind Republican candidates ahead of the November midterms.
Bryson Pace with member station WAER reports the president's rally drew demonstrations.
Protesters gathered by the thousands in downtown Syracuse as President Donald Trump campaigned for Republicans a few blocks away.
Mayor Sharon Owens spoke on behalf of Syracuse, a city the U.S. Census Bureau ranks fourth in the nation for child poverty.
I don't agree with removing SNAP benefits from people who need food security.
I don't agree with the methods for immigration reform.
I believe that there is a process that needs to be improved, but the way it's going now is not protecting us, it's harming us.
A portion of the crowd peeled away to confront Trump's supporters.
They were met by a barricade of police officers and quickly faded.
For NPR News, I'm Bryson Pace in Syracuse, New York.
The United Arab Emirates has released new details in its investigation of a pilot they say tried to hijack a plane full of Israeli passengers.
The incident was deemed an attempted terrorist attack.
NPR's Aya Betrawi reports from Dubai.
The UAE's attorney general says the 29-year-old pilot from Oman had drifted toward extremist ideologies when he was around 20 years old.
They say that's when he started following online content, glorifying suicide attacks while studying in Melbourne.
According to his confession, the UAE says this content influenced his decision to become a pilot.
The UAE says the pilot used two previous flights to Tel Aviv on Fly Dubai to familiarize himself with the route before the September 30 attempted hijacking,
in which investigators say he claims to have acted alone.
The pilot, who was hired by Fly Dubai in January, used an emergency axe to attack the captain before the plane's emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Aya Betrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
This is NPR News in Washington.
The grand prize winners of NPR's student podcast challenge have been announced.
This year's middle and high school champions had a shared interest in how their mind works.
NPR's Janet Ujung Leib reports.
Like millions of Americans, Cora Walsh struggles with reading.
It took years before the seventh grader in Long Island, New York, got a correct diagnosis and started tutoring.
Say "limb."
Limb.
Instead of "room."
Say "sss."
List.
Nice.
Cora's podcast about dyslexia is the middle school podcast challenge winner.
In it, she explains how she sees words and why it's so hard for her to read.
There were entire weeks of my life I barely remember.
What I ate for lunch last Monday.
What assignments I turned in.
What someone said to me in the hallway three Tuesdays ago.
And then, there were moments that somehow just refused to disappear.
High school winner Amit Biligiri in San Jose, California explored a different side of the brain.
Why some memories fade and others stick.
Janet Ujung Leib, NPR News.
OpenAI has fired three safety researchers who say they were dismissed for putting safety ahead of corporate interests.
The maker of ChatGPT says an internal investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information.
The company denies they were fired for raising safety concerns.
The researchers warned the dismissals could discourage employees from speaking openly about AI risks.
They're urging the tech company to honor its commitments to independent safety oversight.
